findings.right_layer: Upstream llvmorg-20.1.8 allowsMisalignedMemoryAccesses (RISCVISelLowering.cpp:21990-22013) is identical minus the fork's '|| hasPULPExtV2()', and untouched in llvmorg-19.1.7..llvmorg-20.1.8. Upstream gives every GPR-held value the scalar answer enableUnalignedScalarMem() (Zicclsm/unaligned-scalar-mem feature, 8a3b6ba7569e) and keeps element alignment for RVV (a5b07a221a57, verified ancestor of 20.1.8). v2i16/v4i8 are GPR values accessed with lw/sw, so the scalar rule is the consistent answer; the fix makes the combine-time legality query agree with LegalizeDAG, which is the correct layer (DAGCombiner is upstream and untouched). Cited fork commit f1b7aebff8c2 exists.
findings.gap9_misaligned_and_perf: GAP9 cores (RI5CY-derived) do execute misaligned lw/sw: GVSoC's ISS splits them (lsu.hpp data_misaligned_req/exec_misaligned, extra latency, CSR_PCER_MISALIGNED counter). The fork does not enable unaligned-scalar-mem for PULP targets, and GAP9 GCC also splits (2 x lh + 2 x sh), so the fix matches the reference compiler. With -mattr=+unaligned-scalar-mem the fixed llc merges the .ll reproducer into one lw/sw (same as int-20), so the hook stays consistent if a GAP9 CPU ever enables the feature. Aligned (>=4) packed accesses never reach this hook (ABI-alignment check first): no performance loss for aligned packed code.
